unit: F135 — link-preview images are hotlinked third-party URLs, leaking viewer IPs

priorAdjudication.claim: CONSTRUCTION_BLOCKED — every remedy requires mirroring/proxying preview images, which enters CH-12 preview-image custody behind G1 leg 5(B).
priorAdjudication.verdict: WRONG, AND WRONG IN A WAY THE DOCTRINE ALREADY FORBIDS.
twoErrors: It used LIVE-CERTIFICATION DEBT as a CONSTRUCTION BLOCKER. G1 leg 5(B) is 'live violating-file refusal not yet observed'. The frozen rule is that certification debt must not hold otherwise-authorized construction hostage.

It treated 'mirror' and 'proxy' as the same act. They are not: one takes third-party bytes into Aura-owned storage and raises storage, retention and copyright questions; the other never stores anything and raises none of them.

adjudication: A — EXECUTABLE NOW. Implemented this pass.
whyG1Leg5BDidNotMatter: Leg 5(B) certifies that the UPLOAD path visibly refuses a violating file — an ingestion/content-truth observation. The F135 remedy touches no ingestion path at all: no upload, no Media row, no object in storage, no derivative, no content-truth classification, no ingestion door. Even setting the doctrine aside, leg 5(B) governs a different subsystem. Setting the subsystem aside, the doctrine forbids the inference anyway.

architectureDiscovered.metadataFetch: aura-backend/src/link-intelligence/link-intelligence.service.ts resolves Open Graph metadata through SafeUrlFetcherService — an SSRF-defended fetcher that re-resolves DNS on every hop, validates each address before a socket opens, checks literal IPs up front, bounds redirects, caps the body and enforces a content-type allowlist.
architectureDiscovered.imageUrlOrigin: LinkPreview.imageUrl / .faviconUrl are lifted verbatim from the linked page's own OG tags — third-party URLs on third-party hosts.
architectureDiscovered.persisted: YES. Both are columns on the LinkPreview row, deduplicated by canonicalUrl and re-fetched only when stale (7 days).
architectureDiscovered.clientFetchedDirectly: YES — this is the defect. conversation_screen.dart rendered Image.network(preview.imageUrl); link_preview_card.dart and internal_reference_card.dart rendered AuraAttachmentImage(url: imageUrl). Each viewer's own client opened a connection to the external host, disclosing IP, user agent and read timing.
architectureDiscovered.notAffected: Share/crawler OG pages source their images from Aura's OWN Media (mediaUrl / mediaLinks), never from LinkPreview — checked, not assumed. Internal-reference cards carry Aura-owned media URLs and were already safe.
architectureDiscovered.custodyAsymmetryFound: Preview METADATA is Aura-custodied (persisted, deduplicated, staleness-managed). Preview IMAGE BYTES had NO custody model at all — the row stored a pointer and the viewer did the fetching. That asymmetry IS the finding.

ch12AuthorityDetermination.category: 3 — REQUIRED INFRASTRUCTURE DID NOT EXIST FOR THIS PATH, BUT POLICY IS ALREADY SETTLED. Implementation work, not a founder blocker.
reasoning: Aura fetching a third-party URL on a member's behalf is ALREADY established and defended: SafeUrlFetcherService exists, is governed, and is the single place that does it. Fetching the image referenced by the very page it already fetched is the same class of act, not a new one.
The remedy adds NO CH-12 custody: no Media row, no R2 object, no derivative, no ingestion door (the ingestion-doors closure test still enumerates exactly the registered doors and passes).

The genuinely unsettled question recorded in the Rich Content contract is OG image MIRRORING — 'privacy gain vs storage/copyright'. Proxying without persistence does not reach it: nothing is stored, so there is no retention policy to write and no copyright position to take.
The remedy therefore changes no frozen CH-12 policy (category 4 does not apply), and needs no policy that does not exist (category 2 does not apply).

solutionChosen.shape: Projections hand the client an Aura URL — GET /v1/link-previews/:id/:kind. The endpoint reads the URL the row already holds, fetches it through the existing SSRF-validated fetcher with an image content-type allowlist and a 5MB ceiling, and streams the bytes back with a 24h Cache-Control so the viewer's browser does the caching. Nothing is written anywhere.
solutionChosen.whyNotMirroring: Mirroring answers the same privacy question but drags in storage, retention and copyright — an explicitly unresolved founder decision. Proxying removes the leak without touching any of it. Smallest mechanism that actually satisfies the finding.
solutionChosen.whyNotAnOpenProxy: The endpoint accepts NO url. It accepts a LinkPreview id and serves only that row's stored URL — a URL Aura's own resolver chose from a page a member linked to. There is no input by which the fetcher can be aimed, so no SSRF surface is added beyond the one that already exists and is already defended.

evaluatedAgainst.viewerPrivacy: The viewer's client now contacts only Aura. The third-party host sees one server-side request, not one per viewer.
evaluatedAgainst.ssrf: Reuses SafeUrlFetcherService — per-hop DNS validation, literal-IP check, redirect bound, timeouts. Non-http(s) schemes are refused before the fetcher is reached.
evaluatedAgainst.contentType: The RESPONSE's own content type decides, never the URL extension. SVG deliberately excluded: a script-bearing document, not a picture.
evaluatedAgainst.payloadLimit: 5MB ceiling — generous for an OG card, small enough that a hostile host cannot use Aura as an amplifier.
evaluatedAgainst.redirects: Bounded at 3 by the shared fetcher, each hop re-validated.
evaluatedAgainst.storageAndRetention: NONE. No new retention doctrine is created because nothing is retained.
evaluatedAgainst.freshness: Follows the existing preview staleness model; no second cache to go stale on its own.
evaluatedAgainst.failureState: Honest 404, no body. The client's existing error path renders nothing. It NEVER falls back to the third-party URL.
evaluatedAgainst.provenance: The row keeps the true source URL unchanged; only what LEAVES the service differs. Site name and canonical URL attribution are untouched.
evaluatedAgainst.abuseAmplification: Bounded by existing LinkPreview rows plus browser caching; no crawling, no URL input.
evaluatedAgainst.duplicatedAuthority: None. One delivery authority, one fetcher, one preview table.

solutionChosen.failClosed: If neither AURA_API_PUBLIC_URL nor RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN is configured, the delivery URL is null and preview images simply do not render. The tempting fallback — emit the original URL — would silently reinstate the exact leak, so it is not done.

authenticationDecision.route: GET /v1/link-previews/:id/:kind is @Public('PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SURFACE'); POST /resolve, which DOES take a URL, stays JwtAuthGuard-protected on the same controller.
authenticationDecision.why: Public posts and announcements render previews to signed-out readers, and a plain network image sends no Authorization header. Requiring a token would blind anonymous readers while leaving them the only viewers still leaking their IP.
authenticationDecision.governance: Declared through the canonical @Public opt-out and added to the reviewed inventory in public-routes.spec.ts, which fails until the inventory is updated deliberately. The fail-closed authentication authority was used, not bypassed.

privacyBeforeAfter.before: Every viewer of every surface carrying a link preview made a direct request to the third-party image host, disclosing IP address, user agent and the timing of their read, once per render.
privacyBeforeAfter.after: The viewer's client requests only Aura. The third-party host is contacted server-side, sees Aura's IP and Aura's user agent, and learns nothing about any viewer.

filesChanged: aura-backend/src/link-intelligence/preview-image-delivery.spec.ts (new — 15 assertions incl. the ratchet + its seeded-failure proof)
aura-backend/src/{announcements,direct-threads,messages,posts,conversations}/... + institutions/posts (8 emission points routed through the authority)
aura-backend/src/{announcements,posts,messages,institutions/posts}/*.link-preview.spec.ts (four specs that had encoded the defect)

ratchet.what: A source scan asserting no file outside the delivery authority reads .imageUrl/.faviconUrl off a linkPreview into a client payload.
ratchet.why: Six services project link previews today; a seventh added tomorrow would reintroduce the leak silently, because nothing about writing linkPreview.imageUrl LOOKS dangerous.
ratchet.fd13: PROVEN ENFORCING — the spec seeds the exact line every projection used to contain and asserts the scanner flags it, then asserts it does not fire on the corrected form.

clientChanges: NONE REQUIRED. The response fields keep their shape and only their value changes, so every surface was fixed at the source rather than six times over.

verification.mediaAndIngestionDoors: 22 suites / 275 tests PASS — no new door, closure test still exact
verification.publicRouteAuthority: PASS with the inventory updated deliberately
verification.frontendSuite: 675 PASS — unchanged, no client change was needed

stateTransition.stage0Preserved: Stage-0 currentState OPEN retained verbatim; this is an execution-layer record.

certificationDebt: Live certification is OWED and NOT claimed: observing on the live system that a preview image renders through the Aura delivery URL and that no request reaches the third-party host. Recorded as debt, which by frozen doctrine does not block construction — the mistake this re-adjudication corrects.

deploymentNote.required: Set AURA_API_PUBLIC_URL on the deployed API (e.g. https://api.auraplatform.org).
deploymentNote.ifOmitted: RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN is used automatically; if neither exists, preview images render as absent rather than leaking. Fails closed either way.
deploymentNote.notPerformed: No production environment was modified by this pass.

founderDecisionsRequired: NONE — existing doctrine settled every choice this remedy required.
